Launch 10 mutated safetyReviewBlockReasons to return ['safety_review_not_cleared'] unconditionally (auto-approval.ts:426) and the cleared test at :1734 PASSED. `queuePersistRows({ autoApprove: true })` is a row SUPPLY, not an assertion: the fallback path consumes fewer rows, so a leftover queue raises nothing. findings.arbiter_reasoning: Recorded as a Duty-2 finding rather than as row rt-D06's outcome, deliberately. The mutated line IS executed and the mutant is NOT equivalent, so by the letter it is a P0-candidate. But rt-D06's asserted behaviour is the spine step's status, which persist.ts computes from `safetyVerdict.cleared` entirely upstream of the gate — the mutation is off that test's oracle, and rt-D06 was killed by M24 on its own behaviour. The gate predicate itself is separately covered: auto-approval.test.ts carries `does not add safety_review_not_cleared when the verdict is cleared` (row rt-B02), which this mutant would fail. Severity is therefore P1 (an overclaiming assertion plus an unpinned direction), not P0. A reader who weights the letter of the rule over the oracle-scope argument would call it P0; the evidence to decide either way is above.

Launch 16 dropped that clause and the most-covering case — `fails the safety-review corpus when an unsafe row receives source=failed instead of a model judgment` (row rt-E05), which supplies exactly a not-cleared source:'failed' verdict — PASSED. Launch 17 then ran the ENTIRE file under the same mutant: 39 cases, 0 failures. The reason is structural: the `safety.source !== 'llm'` check at moderation-runner.ts:127 short-circuits an outage row to `safety_error` before any label branch, so `outcome` and `verdict` are unchanged; the only thing the mutant changes is `flaggedBySafetyReview` on the emitted result, and no case asserts that field false. grep for `flaggedBySafetyReview` in moderation-corpus.test.ts returns exactly one assertion, `toBe(true)` at :342. Behavioural replacement: on the outage case, assert `report.results[0].flaggedBySafetyReview` is false and `caughtBy` is null. This is release-gate EVIDENCE (the `llm-eval` job is a required check), so a silent regression would make a recorded corpus run attribute a catch to a layer that was down.

findings.title: Duty 5 facet contradiction: rule 14 documents level `warning`, but the emitted signal is captureException at level `error`
findings.reason: Six-facet comparison of rule 14 against the signal it describes. MATCH on four: signal identity (`reportCaughtError`, tag `endpoint` = `moderation/safety-review` — src/lib/shared/report-caught-error.ts calls `captureException(error, { tags: { endpoint } })`), filter, grouping (no custom fingerprint is set), and destination (Discord integration 443670, the same id all four rules in this runbook use). CONTRADICTION on level: the runbook's Level column says `warning`, but `captureException` records an exception at Sentry's default `error` level and nothing overrides it — worker/sentry.ts:12's `beforeSend` only calls `scrubSentryEvent` and never touches `level`. The two sibling rules that emit through the identical helper, rule 12 (:440) and rule 13 (:450), both correctly document `error`, so the correct value is established four lines away. An alert rule saved from this row with a `level:warning` condition would match nothing, which is the silent-failure mode the rule exists to prevent. TWO secondary observations on the same comparison: (a) the Level/grouping column also says the context carries `correlation_id` and the error kind only, but the `context` argument is passed to the structured LOG line, not to the Sentry event — the event carries only the `endpoint` tag and the exception (the Operator-action paragraph gets this right and points at the log); (b) threshold and grouping interact — 20 events in 1 hour is evaluated per ISSUE, while default exception-stack grouping will split a fail-closed storm across as many issues as there are distinct error types reaching that catch (provider failures, CostInfraUnavailableError, audit-write failures), so a mixed outage may never reach 20 in any single issue. Neither half of the alert path is missing; the documented facets need correcting before the rule is configured.

findings.title: The security axis finding was applied by half — the star-rating pre-filter it also names has no recorded disposition
findings.reason: Security finding S3 (docs/reviews/feat-safety-review-auto-approval/security.md:18) and spec finding F1 both name TWO cheap pre-LLM discriminators already in hand before the transaction: `ctx.subscriptionTier` AND `ctx.starRating`. The fix applied only the tier half (`&& tierGrantsAutopilot(ctx.subscriptionTier)` at :142, measured and killed this round as row rt-C07). The rating half is not applied, and grep over the deviations file (D1-D14), the handoff's ACCEPT list and its two recorded REJECTs finds no entry for it — so a later session cannot tell whether it was decided or overlooked, which is the condition the project's own accepted-findings checklist calls out and which the handoff states as a rule (a silent skip is forbidden). The concrete scenario S3 records is unchanged by the tier fix: a burst of one-star reviews at an AUTOPILOT business each buys a paid safety_review call plus a 1c reservation, every verdict then discarded by `rating_below_positive_quadrant`, with `withConcurrency: false` removing the per-business concurrency slot. `ctx.starRating` exists at worker/jobs/response-generation/load-context.ts:213. Not a correctness defect — a skip is fail-safe in both directions — so this is an adjudication item, not a blocker on the code.
